Items.Authors: Juan P. Gil, Pedro Silva, Gaspar Fabrega, Nicolas Miranda
Items.Title: ELIANA: an open source library for observatory log analytics
Items.Abstract: ELIANA (Event Log and Incident Analysis) is an open-source Python library for log analytics, developed at the Paranal Observatory to support the analysis of instruments and telescopes. The library is built on top of pandas, allows dataset generation, ML modules, and parlogs-observations, a public dataset of logs for VLTI using the Auxiliary Telescopes distributed as Parquet files aggregated by instrument, time range, and subsystem. ELIANA provides machine learning modules including logistic-regression, Naive-Bayes, specialized tokenizers and NLP utilities. The library has been used to foster academic collaboration (graduate lectures, PhD work, internships) and is actively integrated in several operational tools at Paranal that combine logs with other data sources for troubleshooting and analysis. This contribution presents the architecture of ELIANA, describes the structure and intended use of the parlogs-observations dataset, and illustrates use cases for observatory operations.

Items.Authors: Alfred Miksch, Victoria Laidlaw, Olivier Fauvarque, Benoît Neichel, Ronny Ramlau
Items.Title: Enhanced nonlinear wavefront sensing for adaptive optics with a double iQuad sensor design
Items.Abstract: Advanced adaptive optics (AO) systems use Fourier-type wavefront sensing to correct optical distortions, and  the iQuad wavefront sensor (WFS) is a recent addition to this category. Its four-quadrant phase mask can detect  many wavefront features, but some components may be poorly seen, causing instability in the AO loop. A dual-  path setup using two differently oriented iQuad sensors addresses this limitation by suppressing poorly seen phase  components. To ensure accurate and stable iQuad wavefront sensing, a fast and efficient nonlinear Levenberg-  Marquardt (LM) algorithm is applied for wavefront estimation. Numerical simulations comparing single and  double iQuad configurations show that the dual-sensor approach offers significantly improved performance.

Items.Authors: S. Kendrew, K. Rowlands, M. Engesser, S. Noriega-Crespo, J. Aguilar, S. Alberts, T. Bell, A. Carter, M. Cracraft, M. Decleir, H. Diamond-Lowe, A. Dyrek, K. Gordon, D. Hines, B. Holler, K. Larson, D. Law, K. Murray, B. Nickson, B. O'Sullivan, A. Petric, M. Regan, G. Sloan, B. Sargent, S. Shenoy, B. Trahin, I. Wong
Items.Title: Enhancing the performance and capabilities of the MIRI instrument on JWST
Items.Abstract: MIRI, the Mid-Infrared Instrument on the James Webb Space Telescope, provides the only capability longward of 5 µm on the observatory. In this regime, it is providing order-of-magnitude improvements over past facilities in a wavelength range that is challenging or impossible to access from the ground. As such, MIRI occupies a unique parameter space and offers unparalleled capabilities in all areas of astrophysics. Several years into its operational lifetime, we continue to explore the full breadth of MIRI's potential and make operational improvements to MIRI to create new capabilities and enhance its scientific return. In this paper we will describe several such improvements, and their anticipated impact on MIRI and JWST science - focusing on improvements in detector noise performance, improved time-series capabilities, definition of new subarrays and a wide-field slitless spectroscopy mode.

Items.Authors: Lionel Clermont, Céline Michel, Quentin Chouffart, Yuchen Zhao, Emmanuel Mazy, Ines Fuente, Federico La China, Bertrand Fougnie
Items.Title: Ensuring reliability in space: a closer look at the need for testing multiple optical payload units
Items.Abstract: Spaceborne optical payloads must undergo extensive testing before launch, verifying performance against expectations and generating input data for in-flight software. Recently, a trend has emerged to build multiple units of the same instrument. These can be launched together, increasing the total field of view coverage, or consecutively, extending mission's lifetime beyond that of a single payload and benefiting from economies of scale. This raises a crucial question: Should each model undergo ground testing, or is it sufficient to test just one and apply the findings to all? This presentation will address this question, discussing test and calibration results of 3 supposedly identical payload versions, comparing parameters such as MTF, distortion, polarization spectral properties, and stray light. Our findings indicate that while initial testing offers valuable insights, significant variations among the models necessitate thorough testing of each unit, at least for certain parameters

Items.Authors: Konrad R. Skup, Miroslaw Rataj, Piotr Wawer, Mateusz Sobiecki, Konrad Rutkowski, Przemysław Nita, Grzegorz Szymański, Marianna Fulara, Marcin Sobolewski, Nils Thernstrom, Łukasz Kuryłowicz, Daniel Półtorak, Aleksandra Mirońska, Marek Winkler, Maurycy Ciarka, Adam Sikorski, Roland Ottensamer, Gerald Mösenlechner, Marko Mecina, Armin Luntzer, Warren Holmes, Renaud Goullioud, Mauro Focardi, Eduardo Medinaceli , Raoul Grimoldi
Items.Title: ESA ARIEL FGS: instrument design and implementation
Items.Abstract: In this paper we present the Fine Guiding System (FGS), one of two scientific instruments on board ESA’s ARIEL mission, scheduled for launch in 2029. ARIEL will study hundreds of exoplanets to characterize their atmospheres, investigate chemical composition, cloud properties, and weather variability. FGS serves a dual purpose: it delivers dedicated scientific measurements through three photometric channels and a low-resolution near-infrared spectrometer, while also supporting the spacecraft with ultra-precise pointing. Following the instrument Critical Design Review (iCDR), the FGS has entered the phase of engineering qualification model integration and flight model preparation, marking a major step toward mission readiness.

Items.Authors: Ángela Hernández Delgado, Jorge Quintero Nehrkorn, Fernando Merlos-García, Josué Barrera Martín, Claudia Ruiz de Galarreta, Peter Dr Caligari, Manuel Collados Vera, Carmen Marillai Barreto Cabrera, Hector Socas-Navarro, Sergio Javier Gonzalez Manrique, Miguel Núñez Cagigal
Items.Title: EST Data Centre: challenges
Items.Abstract: The European Solar Telescope (EST) is a 4.2-meter solar facility planned to operate seven instruments: three TIS/FBI systems, three IFS-M units, and the EMBER IFS-S. EST is expected to generate around 169 GiB/s and about 2.7 PiB of data per day, posing major challenges in both data rate and data volume. The data flow from the instruments will require high-performance connectivity at the telescope, while the projected ~80 PiB per year cannot be efficiently handled by a single monolithic data center due to cost, scalability, and reliability limitations. As a result, the EST Data Center (EST-DC) is conceived as a distributed European architecture that minimizes data movement and provides the necessary storage and computing resources, following the FAIR principles

Items.Authors: Maryam Raouph, Andreas Schrimpf
Items.Title: Evaluating natural magnitudes in the photometric system of astronomical plates
Items.Abstract: Accurate photometric calibration of historical astronomical plates is challenging due to mismatched spectral sensitivities with the passbands of modern calibration catalogs. We present a method to derive more accurate and consistent natural magnitudes for plate sources using Gaia DR3 BP/RP low-resolution spectra. By compiling spectral characteristic data for emulsion and filter combinations, and modifying for atmospheric reddening depending on air mass, we compute synthetic magnitudes, utilizing a catalog of Gaia spectral energy distributions (SEDs), via the GaiaXPy python library. This approach overcomes limitations of traditional color term corrections, revealing systematic errors up to ±0.3 mag. It also effectively corrects atmospheric effects at higher air masses (~0.2 mag). This method facilitates integration of historical plate data with modern observations, supporting precise time-domain studies across global photo plate collections.

Items.Authors: Diego Portero-Rodríguez, Nicolás Adrián Rodríguez-Linares, Hugo García-Vázquez, José Javier Díaz García, Luis Fernando Rodríguez Ramos
Items.Title: Evaluating the application of an Integrated photonics wavefront sensor (IP-WFS) using SAOS
Items.Abstract: Solar adaptive optics faces multiple challenges compared with night-time observations. One of these challenges is the low contrast between the Sun and the sky background. This requires the analysis of extended images instead of punctual sources, thereby limiting the spatial resolution in the wavefront sensing and increasing the complexity of the wavefront reconstruction. To overcome this boundary, this group proposed the application of a novel and interesting technology, called integrated photonics or photonics chips, to develop an integrated wavefront sensor, called "Integrated Photonic Wavefront Sensor (IP-WFS)". With the help of the new Solar Adaptive Optics Simulator (SAOS) developed for the EST, this work evaluates the features of the proposed wavefront sensor architecture, the accuracy of the wavefront reconstruction of extended objects for different levels of seeing, as well as technological questions, such as the efficiency of the light injection to single-mode waveguides.

Items.Authors: Durgesh Nandini Satpathy, Jonas Reiffers, Sebastian Albrecht, Thomas Bechteler, Andreas Lederhuber
Items.Title: Evaluation of power conditioning electronics for the satellite-borne x-ray wide field imager of the NewAthena project
Items.Abstract: NewAthena (New Advanced Telescope for High-Energy Astrophysics) is the second large flagship mission of the European Space Agency. NewAthena is planned to house two instruments: the X-IFU (X-ray Integral Field Unit) and the WFI (Wide Field Imager). The development of the WFI is segregated into several subsystems. One of them is the Detector Electronics Subsystem (DES) which contains, inter alia, the Power Conditioning Module (PCM). The PCM is designed to generate stable supply voltages for the WFI Camera Head. This paper outlines the evaluation and optimization of a representative subsection of commandable voltage source circuits on the PCM. The manufactured PCM Evaluation Board (PEB) is subjected to various hardware measurements which are verified using simulation results. Critical parameters, such as the stability of control circuits, function of the complete analog control loop, including the switching mechanism, is simulated and verified by measurements.

Items.Authors: Matthew MacIntosh, Roberto Abuter, Federico Pellegrin
Items.Title: Evolving the methods of displaying real-time data from telescope control software
Items.Abstract: The European Southern Observatory’s (ESO) Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) real-time signal monitoring system has been modernized to replace a legacy architecture based on obsolete VME hardware and Tcl/Tk software. The new solution consolidates data acquisition, transport, and visualization on a single Linux workstation and introduces ESO’s Multicast User Datagram Protocol Interface (MUDPI) as the real-time data distribution layer, which enables seamless streaming of signals from the VLTI reflective memory network. The user interface has been re-implemented in Python using the Qt framework, providing a flexible and responsive environment for signal selection and display.

Items.Authors: Aditya R. Sengupta, Vincent Chambouleyron, Rebecca Jensen-Clem, Emiel Por, Benjamin L. Gerard, Jordan Diaz, Zoe Weber-Porter, Yoo Jung Kim, Steph Sallum, Matthew DeMartino, Daren Dillon, Kevin Bundy, Anna K. Gagnebin, Philip Hinz, Caleb Dobias, Tara Crowe, Stephen S. Eikenberry, Rodrigo Amezcua-Correa, Stephanos Yerolatsitis
Items.Title: Experimentally-determined performance limits for joint imaging and wavefront sensing with a photonic lantern
Items.Abstract: The photonic lantern (PL) is a focal-plane wavefront sensor (WFS) that has been used for second-stage control of extreme adaptive optics (AO) systems. While the number of sensed modes and the dynamic range with respect to each mode have been relatively well characterized, little attention has been paid to the PL's sensitivity, i.e. how measurement noise impacts the accuracy of PL wavefront reconstruction. We compute the PL's sensitivity to photon noise as a function of spatial frequency, and compare it to existing WFSs, using simulations as well as experiments on the muirSEAL testbed. We further assess these metrics in the case where only a subset of PL ports are available for wavefront sensing. This work sets the stage for AO system designs that incorporate the PL as a joint WFS and imager.

Items.Authors: Iremsu Taskin, Jalo Nousiainen, Olivier Absil, Gilles Orban de Xivry, Markus Kasper
Items.Title: Exploring reinforcement learning to enhance focal plane wavefront correction for vortex coronagraphs
Items.Abstract: High Contrast Imaging (HCI) on ground-based telescopes suffers from phase aberrations on the observed wavefront caused by atmospheric turbulence. Adaptive Optics (AO) systems are adept at correcting these aberrations, but fall short in the correction of non-common path aberrations (NCPAs). NCPAs arise because the wavefront sensor (WFS) measures and corrects a wavefront that is different from that affecting the science images, thus requiring additional intervention. This work makes use of focal-plane wavefront sensing and reinforcement learning (RL) to address the wavefront aberrations caused by NCPAs. The PO4NCPA algorithm utilizes sequential phase diversity to address phase ambiguities, and is tested on a simulation designed for the Mid-infrared ELT Imager and Spectrograph (METIS) instrument. Follow-up laboratory testing is conducted in the GHOST bench with the ultimate goal of optimizing RL for on-sky testing.

Items.Authors: Jingyi Zhang, Michael Bottom, Charlotte Guthery, Sébastien Vievard, Antonin Bouchez
Items.Title: Fast and furious on OSIRIS: expanding focal plane wavefront sensing at W. M. Keck Observatory
Items.Abstract: Quasi-static errors, such as non-common path aberrations and co-phasing errors, remain a key limitation to AO performance, and are now the largest part of the AO error budget at W. M. Keck observatory. Fast and Furious is a focal plane wavefront sensing/correction algorithm that runs concurrently with science observations, without requiring any extra hardware, diversity frames, or complex optical models. Now facilitized on NIRC2, it converges within ~5 minutes and consistently delivers Strehl ratio improvements of 10-15%.    We are now funded to expand this algorithm to all Keck AO instruments, and present our first expansion with OSIRIS, an integral field spectrograph and imager. The algorithm typically converges within 10 minutes, showing substantially improved PSF quality. In the future, we plan to expand the functionality of F&F on Keck including 1) its use with laser guide star mode,2) its use with field tracking mode, and 3) use with the new high-order deformable mirror.

Items.Authors: Natasha Popenoe, Benjamin Gerard, Dominic Sanchez
Items.Title: FastrSHWFS development and test results
Items.Abstract: Adaptive Optics (AO) system bandwidth error has been shown to be the dominant error term limiting exoplanet imaging detection sensitivity. We have proposed a solution to improve Shack Hartman wavefront sensor (SHWFS) bandwidth error called the fastrSHWFS, using a custom lenslet array mask to redistribute subapertures from an input circular pupil into a linear or rectangular geometry on the WFS detector to decrease camera read time and thus reduce bandwidth error. In past work fabricated fastrSHWFS lenslet masks had insufficient optical quality; here we present simulation and testing results of new fastrSHWFS masks made by a recently available greyscale two photon polymerization 3D printing technology that in principle provides sufficient depth resolution and dynamic range for such masks.   This work was performed under the auspices of the U.S. Department of Energy by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory under Contract DE-AC52-07NA27344. This document number is LLNL-ABS-2014298.

Items.Authors: Vincenzo Cianniello, Vincenzo De Caprio, Christian Eredia, Enrico Cascone, Marco Riva, Paolo Ciliegi
Items.Title: Finite element analyses of the MORFEO main support structure towards final design review
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI. This paper offers an overview of the finite element analyses of the MORFEO Main Support Structure (MSS) for its structural validation at global level implementing the last mechanical updates. During 2023 MORFEO passed the Preliminary Design Review and now is approaching to Final design review. The models, developed by WP PMO in INAF - Observatory of Naples, are validated through FEM Analysis approach, utilizing CAD (Autodesk Inventor) and CAE (Ansys Workbench) software. In order to have a lighter model for the MORFEO MSS, and shorter computational times, simplified FE model than the whole 3D CAD have been developed. This paper is demonstrated that this method provides accurate results at global level.

Items.Authors: Charles Sallard, Patrice Martinez, Alain Spang, Kian Milani, Lyu Abe
Items.Title: First laboratory demonstration of iEFC for high-contrast imaging at small angular separation on ELT scales
Items.Abstract: Implicit Electric Field Conjugation (iEFC) is a model-free wavefront control method that creates and maintains dark holes using real calibration data. We present the first demonstration of iEFC at very small angular separations, producing a 1–4 λ/D dark hole on a segmented pupil in H band using the SPEED testbed.  SPEED’s ELT-oriented design, including a reflective PIAACMC coronagraph and multi-plane DM architecture, enables compact dark holes at aggressive IWAs. These results demonstrate that combining iEFC with SPEED’s WFC architecture provides a valuable R&D pathway toward future ELT-class high-contrast instruments, ultimately aiming to reach contrasts on the order of 10⁻⁷.

Items.Authors: Anthony Meilland, Florentin Millour, Jeronimo Calderon Gomez, Stéphane Lagarde, Julien Dejonghe
Items.Title: First laboratory results from SPINER echelle interferometry and prospects for future instrumentation
Items.Abstract: Spectro-interferometry enables detailed studies of astrophysical objects by probing their geometry as well as their physical, chemical, and dynamical properties across different wavelengths, but current instruments are limited in either spectral resolution or bandwidth. To overcome these limitations, we introduced SPINER in 2024, a concept based on Echelle dispersion for spectro-interferometry, and developed the first visible multi-order test bench covering 600–900 nm at a high spectral resolution of R=20,000. Here, we present our first in-lab results, characterize the prototype’s performance, and discuss prospects for implementing SPINER in the visible and near-infrared on facilities such as the VLTI and CHARA arrays, opening new opportunities for high-resolution studies of stars, disks, and exoplanetary systems.

Items.Authors: D. Lancaster, S. Chhabra, S. Kraus, J. Paul, O. Snaith
Items.Title: F-number characterisation of a photonics integrated optics device
Items.Abstract: BIFROST combines the four beams produced by the Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) into a spectrograph in the near-infrared (1-1.7um). To combine the light of the four beams it was proposed and contracted to use a integrated optics chip to combine the light of four beams and produce an interferometric signal using the ABCD method. This report details the acceptance testing and methodology used to verify the performance of preliminary test devices.

Items.Authors: Amna Waris, Chris Waring, Bradley Frank, Noah Schwartz, Charlotte Bond, Maxime Dumont, Douglas Harvey, Ilgin Okan, Maia Jones
Items.Title: FPGA accelerated machine learning for adaptive optics: a hardware-in-the-loop prototype
Items.Abstract: This work presents a hardware-in-the-loop prototype built on the AMD Versal Vision platform that pairs live sensor input with on device machine learning inference to investigate compact, embedded approaches to AO processing. The prototype builds on two earlier hardware demonstrators: a real-time imaging pipeline on an AMD Kintex UltraScale, and a machine-learning regression model for mirror alignment that achieved wavefront errors of around 6 nm RMS when deployed on a Versal AI Core. By integrating these strands, the system provides a platform for testing embedded ML pipelines under AO-relevant timing conditions and exploring their potential use in future low-power AO architectures.

Items.Authors: Joshua Liberman, Sebastiaan Y. Haffert, Jared R. Males, Aditya Khandelwal, Stephanie Rinaldi, Jay Kueny, Katie Twitchell, Joseph D. Long, Ewan S. Douglas, Lauren Schatz, Jennifer Lumbres
Items.Title: Freezing the speckles: focal plane wavefront sensing with the Spatially Clipped Self-Coherent Camera
Items.Abstract: The Extremely Large Telescopes (ELTs) and the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) require active speckle suppression to directly image exo-Earths. Focal plane wavefront sensing and control (WFSC) allows us to detect and remove time-varying speckles. The self-coherent camera (SCC) modifies a standard coronagraph design, creating a reference electric field that interferes with speckles in the final focal plane to form Fizeau fringes. However, the classic SCC needs oversized optics, limiting its implementation. We propose a new variant, the Spatially-Clipped Self-Coherent Camera (SCSCC). Our SCSCC reduces overall beam footprint and boosts sensor resolution by 3x. We present the SCSCC optical design combined with the photon-resolving Hamamatsu camera. We demonstrate high speed WFSC and active dark hole maintenance with the SCSCC in the lab, exploring the sensor’s robustness to time-varying speckles. The SCSCC is a valuable wavefront sensor for the upcoming HWO mission and the next-gen ELTs.

Items.Authors: Alan W. McConnachie, David Del Rizzo, Alexis Hill, Scott Roberts
Items.HTMLTitle: From blue skies to the night sky: tracking R&D heritage that enables world observatories
Items.Title: From blue skies to the night sky: tracking R&D heritage that enables world observatories
Items.Abstract: With the construction of the Square Kilometer Array (SKA) at radio wavelengths, the Extremely Large Telescopes (ELTs) at OIR wavelengths, and the ongoing scientific exploitation of the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) at mm/submm wavelengths, it is clear that astronomy is in the era of world observatories. None of these observatories or instruments would exist – and none of their future instruments will exist – without investment in strategic R&D by observatories and other groups to enable the next generation of instruments. I present case studies from the NRC Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Center – including radio correlators and receiver components, antenna design, and adaptive optics – to track the evolution of certain technologies from blue-sky concepts all the way to deployment on premier international facilities, where I try to identify commonalities, from how the idea was generated to key moments in the development pipeline.

Items.Authors: Kangning Wang, Sizhe Wen, Jing Chen, Yanlei Wen, Zhiguo Jiang, Danpei Zhao, Haopeng Zhang
Items.Title: From raw telemetry to calibrated space-object catalogs: a self-calibrating pipeline for a space-based star-field imager
Items.Abstract: Space-based optical sensors are becoming an important component of space situational awareness (SSA), but their data processing chains are often fragmented across separate decoding, calibration, detection, and photometry tools, which complicates uniform deployments for on-orbit experiments and small demonstration payloads. We present an integrated, catalog-driven data reduction pipeline for space-based star-field imagery that produces astrometrically and photometrically calibrated space-object catalogs directly from downlinked telemetry. The pipeline outputs a structured space-object catalog containing pixel coordinates, sky coordinates, and brightness estimates, and is implemented as a modular software system suitable for both ground-based post-processing and future on-board deployment.

Items.Authors: Daniel S. Dahl, Nathan K. Long, Barnaby Norris, Christopher H. Betters, Akira Rodziewicz-Ryan, Jin Wei, Sergio Leon-Saval
Items.Title: From simulation to demonstration: hybrid mode-selective photonic lanterns for simultaneous optimal fibre injection and wavefront sensing
Items.Abstract: Photonic lanterns convert a multimode point-spread function at the telescope focal plane into multiple stable single-mode outputs that encode the incident wavefront, enabling sensitive focal-plane wavefront sensing. Hybrid mode-selective photonic lanterns (HMS-PLs) extend this concept by isolating the fundamental mode into a dedicated output while allowing the higher-order modes to be sensed separately and used to drive an adaptive-optics system for zero-NCPA, optimised single-mode injection.  We report the first fabrication and H-band laboratory characterisation of an HMS-PL and compare the results with Lightbeam simulations. The strong agreement between measurement and simulation demonstrates the viability of HMS-PLs as both efficient mode filters and powerful wavefront-diagnostic elements, supporting their use in future astronomical instruments such as Seidr within the ASGARD suite at the VLTI.

Items.Authors: J. J. D. Luis, J. Altamirano, J. P. L. G. Barrios, D. F. Buscher, M. J. Creech-Eakman, E. K. R. Floyd, C. A. Haniff, J. C. Mason, A. Olivares, S. Rochelle, C. Salcido, R. Santoro, I. Schofield, J. S. Young
Items.Title: Full-system performance verification results for the Magdalena Ridge Observatory Interferometer’s first two beamlines
Items.Abstract: First stellar fringes at the Magdalena Ridge Observatory Interferometer (MROI) were achieved in July 2025 using a 7.9 m baseline. We have measured the optical performance of the full individual beamlines and aspects of the system as a whole. In this paper we describe the current performance of the MROI in terms of key metrics that typically limit the sensitivity of interferometric measurements, such as static wavefront error, optical throughput, beam alignment jitter/drift and piston jitter. We highlight the remaining issues that we hope to overcome to reach the predicted limiting magnitude of our first science combiner, FOURIER, of 13 in the H band.

Items.Authors: Jacob Trzaska, Amit Ashok
Items.Title: Fundamental limits to wavefront sensing with resolved guide stars
Items.Abstract: We present fundamental limits to wavefront sensing when a telescope's guide star is partially resolved and the adaptive optics-corrected optical field is weakly aberrated, i.e., we are operating in the "high-Strehl regime." Illustrative simulation examples are shown for a toy model of the Giant Magellan telescope, where we investigate the minimally achievable phase and amplitude reconstruction errors, as well as methods for saturating the respective limits.

Items.Authors: Hong-yu Jin, Qi Feng, Hui Wang, Hong-fei Zhang, Jian Wang
Items.HTMLTitle: Gain measurement and uncertainty analysis using 55 Fe x-ray sources and photon transfer curves
Items.Title: Gain measurement and uncertainty analysis using 55Fe x-ray sources and photon transfer curves
Items.Abstract: Gain, defined as the average number of electrons generated by incident photons per digital number (DN) unit at the output stage of a CCD-detector, constitutes a critical performance metric. The two mainstream characterization methods are Radioisotope Method and Photon Transfer Curve (PTC) Method. Comparatively, The PTC method offers faster testing speeds, while the radioisotope method achieves higher measurement accuracy.   We design an experimental setup for gain measurement based our test camera. In the Fe⁵⁵ source test, a Dewar lid with an internally installed Fe⁵⁵ source and robotic arm is used. In the PTC test, a glass-equipped Dewar lid is employed, placed at one end of the light-tight box, while an adjustable uniform light source is positioned at the other end.  We employ both techniques to measure the gain of a CCD290-99 camera and conduct a comparison with systematic uncertainty quantification.

Items.Authors: Xue Cheng, Yonghe Chen, Yutian Fu
Items.Title: Gain measurement method for CMOS detectors based on a modified photon transfer curve
Items.Abstract: The Earth 2.0 (ET) mission requires extreme image quality and photometric stability from its scientific CMOS detector, relying on precise photon transfer curve (PTC) gain calibration. Traditional PTC methods ignores nonlinear response and fixed-pattern noise, which introduces systematic errors—especially under low-light conditions and across the full dynamic range.  To overcome this, we propose an improved PTC-based gain calculation method. A highly stable monochromatic light source first calibrates the nonlinear response, enabling a pre-correction that removes associated bias. Pixel-level temporal variance analysis is also applied to suppress fixed-pattern noise in PTC fitting.  Simulations and experiments confirm that this method significantly improves detector characterization confidence and offers more accurate gain results. The approach provides a reliable theoretical foundation for developing and evaluating ultra-high-precision space imaging systems.

Items.Authors: Akito Kutsumi
Items.Title: Geant4 simulation of magnetic diverter for the wide field view X-ray monitor on HiZ-GUNDAM
Items.Abstract: Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs) are transient phenomena that release energy on the order of 10^52 ergs. The HiZ-GUNDAM project is a future satellite mission aimed at contributing to multi-messenger astronomy and early universe exploration through observations of GRBs. The HiZ-GUNDAM satellite operates in a sun-synchronous orbit to satisfy the temperature requirements of MONSTER. However, this orbit includes the auroral oval and the South Atlantic Anomaly, where many electrons exist. These electrons and their secondary particles increase the background. In the auroral oval, where electron flux is particularly high, for efficient detection by EAGLE, address the electron background with (i) choosing the thickness and material of the EAGLE housing wall, and (ii) the installation of a magnet diverter that prevents electron incidence on the detector by Lorentz force. In this talk, we report on progress of electron background estimation and countermeasure studies using Geant4 simulations.

Items.Authors: Marco Feroci, Yuri Evangelista, Riccardo Campana, Alessio Trois, Alessandra De Rosa, Alessio Nuti, Francesco Ceraudo, Ettore Del Monte, Gianluigi Zampa, Melania Del Santo, Stefano Bianchi, Gianluca Israel, Giulia Stratta, Stefano Vercellone, Natalia Auricchio, Mauro Fiorini, Gianluca Morgante, Paolo Nogara, Matias Antonelli, Giuseppe Bertuccio, Marco Grassi, Ugo Lo Cicero, Paolo Zuccon, Giovanni Ambrosi, Matteo Bachetti, Om Salafia, Luigi Stella, Giovanni Della Casa, Giovanni Lombardi, Edoardo Giancarli, Luigi Pacciani, Giancarlo Ghirlanda, Filippo D'Ammando, Alessandra Lamastra, Alessandro Papitto, Patrizia Romano, Giovanni Morlino, Antonino D'Ai
Items.Title: GECO: galactic and extragalactic compact-object observatory
Items.Abstract: GECO is a mission concept recently submitted to a Small National Mission call jointly issued by  INAF (the Italian National Institute for Astrophysics) and ASI (Italian Space Agency) for a fast-track (5 years)  space mission, including a scientific payload not in excess of 100 kg and technologies with TRL >=5.    GECO proposes an unprecedented combination of field of view (half-sky), point source location   accuracy (1 arcmin), broad spectral response (2 keV – 2 MeV) and energy resolution (350 eV at 6 keV).   The GECO scientific paylaod is composed of 2 instruments.  The GECO coded-mask All Sky Monitor (ASM, 2–50 keV) will detect, localize and study steady,   variable and transient sources simultaneously appearing anywhere in the accessible 50% of the sky,   downlinking real-time arcmin-accurate localizations and photon-by-photon data for deeper spectral   and timing studies.   The Broadband Universal Radiation Spectrometer for Transients (BURST) instrument will extend   the energy band of GECO up

Items.Authors: Giulio Capasso, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Marco Baldini, Andrea Balestra, Massimiliano Belluso, Andrea Bulgarelli, Alessandro Cabras, Marco Citossi, Mirko Colapietro, Stefano Giovannini, David Goz, Marco Landoni, Enrico Licata, Ugo Lo Cicero, Sara Elisa Motta, Amedeo Petrella, Simone Riggi, Salvatore Savarese, Francesco Schillirò, Pietro Schipani, Riccardo Smareglia, Roberto Vecchiato
Items.Title: Generative AI: strategies and use cases for astronomy
Items.Abstract: Generative AI promises to revolutionize astrophysics and astronomical instrumentation, yet its adoption requires systemic governance to ensure scientific reproducibility. This presentation details the strategy of Gen.IA, a study group at the Italian National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF), designed to bridge the gap between experimental AI and operational deployment.    We present preliminary results from an internal survey assessing AI adoption, expectations, and ethical sentiment within INAF. We further outline a strategic roadmap focusing on knowledge sharing, staff upskilling, and regulatory compliance. Key use cases under investigation include Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for complex technical documentation, AI-driven requirement management in systems engineering, Agentic AI for automated data analysis, and AI-assisted literature review. This work offers a pathway to leverage Generative AI while balancing innovation with scientific integrity.

Items.Authors: Peter M. Thompson, Hugo Chiquito
Items.Title: GMT finite element analysis: state space versus second order form
Items.Abstract: Finite element models are routinely used to design and analyze telescope structures and optical mechanical subsystems. Computational time saving methods are described for both temporal and frequency domain analysis. The standard practice in the telescope design community is to convert the second order model to first order state space form. The preference described here is to stay with the second order form, where for high order problems the computational time can be reduced from hours to minutes, even seconds. These methods are documented here for the wider telescope community

Items.Authors: Timothy Chin, Zhemin Cai, Ali Ghari Zadeh, Jonathan Moller, Dylan Simpfendorfer, Helen McGregor, Yizheng Wang, Jon Lawrence, Nick Cerneaz, Dani Guzman, Jake Linden, Chris Coote, Jessica Zheng
Items.Title: GNAO AOB: mechanical design of an adaptive optics bench for Gemini North
Items.Abstract: Gemini North Adaptive Optics (GNAO) is a next generation AO system for the 8-metre Gemini North telescope, replacing the existing Altair AO system. The GNAO Adaptive Optics Bench (AOB) will be installed on port 4 of the instrument support structure and houses the deformable mirror and wavefront sensors. AOB will serve to enable GLAO and LTAO within a corrected field of view of 2 arcmin. GNAO is being designed in tandem with the downstream instrument GIRMOS and is planned to go on sky at the same time. The wavefront sensing path includes a laser guide star camera which supports 4 lasers in a 30 arcsec asterism as well as two natural guide star cameras to provide tip tilt and slow focus corrections.    This paper presents the overall mechanical design of the AOB, details on the support structure that houses the electronics cabinets and analysis of the thermal management of the electronics.

Items.Authors: Gwyneth Lannon, Jeffrey Chilcote, Joel Burke, Vincent Chambouleyron, Robert De Rosa, Clarissa R. Do Ó, Jennifer Dunn, Matthew Engstrom, Joeleff Fitzsimmons, Oyku Galvan, Randall Hamper, Dan Kerley, Quinn M. Konopacky, Bruce Macintosh, Christian Marois, Teo Mocnik, Eric Nielsen, Jayke S. Nguyen, Dillon Peng, Saavidra Perera, Brian Sands, Dmitry Savransky, Nicole Wolff
Items.Title: GPI 2.0: detector status and potential new data analysis method for the Gemini Planet Imager
Items.Abstract: The Gemini Planet Imager (GPI) is a facility-class high-contrast imaging instrument designed for the direct detection and characterization of exoplanets. Following its time at the Gemini South Observatory, it is currently undergoing an upgrade to GPI 2.0. Among the systems receiving an upgrade is GPI’s integral field spectrograph (IFS). Since GPI’s removal from Gemini South, the detector in its IFS has deteriorated considerably, and has been replaced as part of the upgrade. This paper will present an account of the old detector’s deterioration from 2014 (the start of GPI’s time at Gemini South) through 2025 and, if available, preliminary performance of the new detector. We will also explore a potential new data analysis method which would allow us to take advantage of the new detector’s increased capabilities.

Items.Authors: Hugo Gaquere, Cyril Tasse, Olivier Aumage, Damien Gratadour
Items.Title: GPU accelerated deconvolution of radio-interferometric data
Items.Abstract: Deconvolution in modern radio-interferometric imaging pipelines face severe performance constraints: deconvolution represents a bottleneck and current implementations lack of portability. We propose a modular GPU-accelerated framework for radio-astronomy deconvolution, to improve runtime performance, portability across pipelines and to reduce algorithm implementation overhead.

Items.Authors: Yan Li, Xinyu Yao, Jian Ge, Jianqing Cai, Pengjun Zhang, Congcong Zhang
Items.Title: Ground-based simulation and validation of GSENSE 1081BSI CMOS detectors for ultra-high-precision photometry in the Earth 2.0 Space Mission
Items.Abstract: The Earth 2.0 (ET) space mission requires ultra-high photometric precision (~84 ppm) to detect Earth-like planets around Sun-like stars via the transit method. This paper presents a ground-based simulation experiment designed to evaluate whether the GSENSE 1081BSI CMOS detectors can meet the mission’s photometric performance requirements.The evaluation focused on three key performance metrics: long-term photometric precision, temporal stability, and the ability to recover injected 84 ppm transit signals of Earth 2.0s. Simulated transit events were introduced into the data to directly assess detection capability at the required precision level. The results demonstrate that the GSENSE 1081BSI detectors satisfy the photometric performance re

Items.Authors: Alexis Carlotti, Steven Martos, Laurent Jocou, Stéphane Curaba, Edgard Renault, Pierre Janin-Potiron, Yves Magnard, Thibaut Moulin, Laly Boyer, Jean-François Sauvage, Charlotte Bond, Kjetil Dohlen, Benoit Neichel, Anne Costille, David Le Mignant, Mickael Bonnefoy, Arthur Vigan, Philippe Delorme, Elodie Choquet
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT: from design trade-offs to prototypes of the high-contrast capability
Items.Abstract: HARMONI is the first light, adaptive optics assisted,  near-IR integral field spectrograph for the ELT. It covers a spectral range from 800nm to 2450nm with resolving powers from 3000 to 7000 and spatial sampling of 25mas and 6mas. It can operate in two adaptive optics modes - SCAO (including a high contrast capability) and MCAO. The project is resuming its final design phase after a rescope design phase in 2025. The high-contrast (HC) system will enable observations of exoplanets and disks as close as 35mas from the star, and will transmit light from 1250nm up to 2450nm. At 200mas, it will enable the detection of companions displaying a 1e-6 flux ratio (or lower) with the star, using post processing techniques such as ADI, SDI and spectral cross-correlation. We will present an updated view of the system and the new properties of the apodizers and focal plane masks, as well as results obtained in the laboratory with the engineering model of the ZELDA WFS.

Items.Authors: Johan D. Floriot, Thomas Pichon, Kjetil Dohlen, Jean-François Sauvage, Zalpha Challita, William Bon, Anne Bonnefoi, Alexandre Bozier, Anne Costille, David Le Mignant, Rémi Lamble
Items.Title: HARMONI at ELT: SCAOS design and development plan after rescope
Items.Abstract: HARMONI is the first light, adaptive optics assisted, near-IR integral field spectrograph for the ELT. It covers a spectral range from 800nm to 2450nm with resolving powers from 3000 to 7000 and spatial sampling of 25mas and 6mas. It can operate in two adaptive optics modes - SCAO (including a high contrast capability) and MCAO. The project is resuming its final design phase after a rescope design phase in 2025.  The updated SCAOS optomechanical design will be presented and discussed. We will also introduce our staggered SCAOS development strategy and detail the design and analysis for each of the modules that we intend to develop and test prior to the system integration: pyramid module, low order adaptive optics loop, ADC module, derotator.

Items.Authors: Anabel Romero, Chiaki Crews, Ben Dryer, Angaraj Duara, Jason Gow, David Hall, Douglas Jordan, Joan Requena, Jesper Skottfelt
Items.Title: Heavy ion testing of a CMOS image sensor for future space telescope missions
Items.Abstract: Future space telescope missions require high-resolution detectors that can measure light with a wide range of wavelengths. CMOS image sensors are being considered for such telescopes, with Teledyne e2v’s CIS300 family being a prime candidate. The CIS300 is a large area CMOS detector that detects light in the ultraviolet, visible, and near infrared. Missions such as ARRAKIHS and CASTOR, which aim to study dark matter and galaxy formation, have chosen the CIS300 as its main detector. Other missions considering the CIS300 include NASA’s Habitable Worlds Observatory, which aims to study earth-like planets. The various settings and modes of operation of the CIS300 require testing, characterisation, and optimisation, for which a setup was developed. Additionally, a heavy ion test was done on a CIS303 4.5k detector to simulate the impact of cosmic rays for space qualification. Testing of the CIS300 is underway, enabling the detector technologies necessary for future space telescope missions.

Items.Authors: Salvador Cuevas, Mamadou Ndiaye, Arthur Vigan, Paula Betancourt Esparza, Luis A. Martinez Hernandez, Leonardo Garcés, Carolina Keiman, Beatriz Sanchez, Luis Alvarez-Nuñez, Oscar Chapa, Ruben Flores, Carlos Espejo, Gerardo Lara
Items.Title: High contrast high resolution integral field spectroscopy with GTC/FRIDA for the study of gas giant exoplanets
Items.Abstract: We explore the potential of FRIDA, on the Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC), to study young gas giant exoplanets. FRIDA is an imager and integral field spectrograph (IFS) which will operate in the near-infrared (0.9-25m) in concert with GTCAO, the adaptive optics (AO) system of GTC. The instrument provides three pixel/spaxel scales: 10, 20, and 40 mas. In its IFS mode, FRIDA features two resolutions: (i) medium (R1500-4000) in the z, J ,H, K bands and (ii) high (R30000) in H and K bands. Additionally, FRIDA exhibits high-contrast capabilities in both imaging and IFS. Among the wide range of science cases, FRIDA is expected to observe young gas giant planets thanks to the combination of the AO corrected beam, coronagraphs, and high-spectral resolution IFS. With its IFS data cube and cross-correlation techniques, FRIDA should be able to identify the presence of molecules in the atmosphere of exoplanets.

Items.Authors: Emanuele Taralli, Sven Visser, Roland Den Hartog, Paul Van der Hulst
Items.Title: High-accuracy cryogenic thermometry via Mott variable-range hopping for Athena/X-IFU
Items.Abstract: We present a compact calibration method for cryogenic NTC thermistors based on the Mott variable-range hopping (MVRH) model, providing an accurate resistance–temperature relation from 40 mK to 40 K. By fitting R(T) with only a few coefficients and inverting it through a truncated Puiseux expansion, the method enables reliable temperature extraction from measured resistance values. Applied to RuO₂ and Ge sensors, it achieves relative residuals ≤1–1.7%, outperforming common polynomial or exponential calibrations while avoiding instability at low temperature. The approach remains robust for sparse datasets and ensures consistent calibration across multiple cryogenic stages. This physically grounded framework is well suited for space instruments requiring precise thermometry, such as the Athena X-IFU Focal Plane Assembly.

Items.Authors: Matthew Heine, Catherine E. Grant, Marshall W. Bautz, Beverly J. LaMarr, Eric D. Miller, David Hall, Michael Hubbard, Joan Requena, Emanuele Perinati, Steven W. Allen, Artem Poliszczuk, Dan Wilkins, Fabio Gastaldello, Silvano Molendi, Ralph Kraft, Gerrit Schellenberger, Arnab Sarkar
Items.Title: High-statistics simulations of NewAthena WFI background using Geant4
Items.Abstract: The observation of hot gas structures is one science goal of the Wide Field Imager (WFI) on ESA’s NewAthena X-ray observatory. Because the measurement of these faint diffuse sources is limited by background from cosmic ray particle interactions within the instrument, understanding and reducing this background is critical. To this end, we employ a two-pronged approach, performing high-fidelity Geant4 simulations on both detailed, realistic geometry models as well as complementary simple geometry models. The former can reveal subtle sensitivities of background to details of the instrument design. The latter allows for fast iteration, useful in guiding and understanding the larger simulations. We show how we leverage High Performance Computing resources to achieve simultaneously high throughput and fast time to result. We discuss our recent results, which are applicable to not only WFI, but also other X-ray missions.

Items.Authors: Dhiraj Gupta, Andrea Bianco, Michele Frangiamore, Davide Giughello, Laura Schreiber, Eric Stadler, Emiliano Diolaiti
Items.Title: Holographic diffuser for future applications in astronomical instrumentation
Items.Abstract: Volume Holographic Optical Elements (VHOEs) are specialized components that use recorded interference patterns to shape light wavefronts and they could find applications in modern astronomical instruments where conventional optics cannot easily handle. In adaptive optics (AO) for telescopes, pyramid wavefront sensors need dynamic beam modulation for sensitivity, making the system susceptible to misalignment. In this paper, we present innovative VHOEs that specifically address these challenges. We developed a volume holographic diffuser that offers static wavefront modulation, which can reduce alignment sensitivity in a pyramid AO sensor. This single diffractive element achieves the required small scattering angle with higher diffraction efficiency, meeting the design goals for next-generation astronomical instruments.

Items.Authors: Jose Schiappacasse Ulloa, Laura Magrini, Anna Brucalassi, Sofia Randich, Letizia Caito, Enrico Giro, Marco Riva, Andrea Bianco, Michele Frangiamore
Items.Title: HRMOS: initial development of the exposure time calculator
Items.Abstract: We present the Exposure Time Calculator (ETC) currently under development for HRMOS, the High-Resolution Multi-Object Spectrograph. The HRMOS ETC delivers quantitative predictions of instrument performance across a wide range of observational setups and environmental conditions, enabling accurate estimates of signal-to-noise ratios and exposure times. As a result, it plays a central role throughout the project lifecycle—from guiding instrument design and optimisation to supporting the preparation and planning of scientific observations. We outline the ETC framework, its implementation strategy, and its relevance for maximising the scientific return of HRMOS.

Items.Authors: Ivan Agostinelli, Alessandro Di Filippo, Lorenzo Paonni, Mauro Centrone, Marco Faccini
Items.Title: Hybrid AI optimization for sensorless adaptive optics
Items.Abstract: This work presents an AI-augmented, fully sensorless adaptive optics (AO) framework designed to overcome atmospheric turbulence and reduce the computational burden of real-time correction. The system builds upon ZARA, a metaheuristic wavefront-optimization algorithm that iteratively adjusts Zernike coefficients using a Fourier-based image-quality metric. To accelerate convergence, a lightweight neural pre-conditioner provides a coarse estimate of the corrected point-spread function, narrowing the solution space explored by ZARA. A downstream local optimization module further refines the output through fine-tuning. This three-stage architecture improves robustness, accuracy, and convergence speed, offering a flexible and generalizable closed-loop AO strategy.

Items.Authors: David Rodríguez Muñoz, Mario Manzano Garcia, Samuel Sordo Ibañez, Carlos Colodro, Jose Carlos Sanluis Leal, Gara Ramos, Luis Guirado Fuentes, Pablo González de Chaves, Marco Michelle Bellisario, Xana Delpueyo Español, Jose Alonso Burgal, Alfonso Ynigo Rivera, Álex Oscoz
Items.Title: IACSAT-DUNE: preliminary pointing jitter characterization and its impact on exoplanet photometry
Items.Abstract: In the context of the IACSAT-DUNE mission, the IAC is  studying the impact of pointing jitter on photometric  performance caused by sensor non-uniformity. To  better understand this noise source, the team is  combining analytical modeling with laboratory  experiments. The results from this study will establish  the core requirements for the payload-level Pointing  and Focus Control System (PFCS) currently under  development.

Items.Authors: Pierpaolo Merola, Marina Vela Nunez, Vladimiro Noce, Mauro Focardi, Luca Carbonaro, Edoardo Rossi, Simone Chiarucci, Marianna Michelagnoli, Elisabetta Giani, Gianluca Marotta, Paolo Chioetto, Paolo Picchi, Paola Zuppella, Fulvio De Persio
Items.Title: ICU to TCU interface emulator for the ARIEL Telescope Assembly thermal-vacuum test: hardware and communication logic
Items.Abstract: To read telemetry and command the actuators of the ARIEL Telescope Assembly during thermal-vacuum chamber tests, an Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE) has been developed to interface with the Telescope Control Unit (TCU), replacing the entire communication chain up to and including the connection with the Instrument Control Unit. The TCU gathers all temperature-sensor telemetry and its own housekeeping data. It is also responsible for driving the Secondary Mirror Mechanism and monitoring its status. Nominal communication with the TCU is established using an Arduino Due board and a Low-voltage differential signaling module integrated inside a dedicated enclosure. The link between the EGSE and the TCU is established through a differential-signal interface based on the SPI protocol. The final system was assembled and tested using the full TCU simulator at the INAF - Arcetri Astrophysics Observatory.

Items.Authors: Marina Vela Nuñez, Pierpaolo Merola, Mauro Focardi, Vladimiro Noce, Luca Carbonaro, Simone Chiarucci, Elisabetta Giani, Gianluca Marotta, Paolo Chioetto, Paolo Picchi, Paolo Zuppella, Marianna Michelagnoli, Edoardo Rossi, Fulvio De Persio
Items.Title: ICU to TCU interface emulator for the ARIEL Telescope Assembly thermal-vacuum test: software and graphical user interface
Items.Abstract: This paper presents the software modules developed for the “ARIEL ICU–TCU Interface Emulator” (EGSE), designed to support the thermal-vacuum (TVAC) test campaign of the Telescope Assembly of ESA’s ARIEL mission. The emulator implements the ICU–TCU communication link, enabling decoding of telemetry packets, telecommand handling, and the monitoring and control of the TCU during test operations. The GUI provides an integrated environment for configuration, real-time visualization, actuator motion control, telemetry supervision, and automated test procedures. The system was validated first with a data-packet simulator and later with the full TCU simulator at INAF-Arcetri. The emulator enhances test execution efficiency, data accessibility, and provides a scalable framework for future operational procedures.

Items.Authors: Juhyeong Kim, Dae-Hee Lee, Chae Kyung Sim
Items.Title: Image recognition using onboard AI for space exploration: from Raspberry Pi validation to a mission-suitable model
Items.Abstract: In space exploration missions, onboard AI has been proposed for autonomous data analysis and improved mission  efficiency. However, conventional GPU systems are difficult to deploy on spaceborne platforms due to high power  consumption and radiation vulnerability. Instead, spacecraft often utilizes low-power, radiation-tolerant hardware,  with limited computational capacity. Therefore, onboard AI requires lightweight and efficient architecture.  In this study, the feasibility of onboard AI was initially validated by demonstrating object detection  on Raspberry Pi 4B using YOLOv5n at a watt-level power consumption. The model was then adapted to directly  process raw, single-channel intensity data from spacecraft imaging instruments without channel replication,  which successfully improved both accuracy and speed over conventional three-channel configurations. Finally,  a lightweight super-resolution model was integrated; despite slight speed drop, it enhanced object detection  performance.

Items.Authors: Been Yeo, Jiwoo Lee, Hyung-Chul Lim, Kyohoon Ahn
Items.Title: Implementation of an adaptive optics system for free-space optical communication-based quantum key distribution
Items.Abstract: This study aims to implement an adaptive optics (AO) system for free-space optical (FSO) communication-based quantum key distribution (QKD). The exponential increase in data generated by space telescopes and satellites necessitates high-speed and secure data transfer in satellite-ground links. However, atmospheric turbulence causes severe wavefront distortion and beam spreading, drastically reducing coupling efficiency. To ensure stable links, we developed a real-time AO system for an FSO-QKD system. The system measures wavefronts using a Shack-Hartmann Wavefront Sensor with a 19x19 lenslet array and corrects distortion using a Deformable Mirror with 308 actuators (20x20 actuators array). The closed-loop control algorithm uses Zernike polynomials to analyze and minimize aberrations. We have validated the system's performance in a laboratory environment and plan on-sky performance verification using the 1 m telescope at the Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute (KASI).

Items.Authors: Solange V. Ramírez, Stephen C. Hope, Leon Aslan, Robert Barkhouser, Christoph Birk, Julia Brady, Maren Cosens, Tyson Hare, Charlie Hull, Karim Kaismoune, Daniel D. Kelson, Gerrad Killion, Konidaris P. Nicholas, Alicia Lanz, Jacob McCloskey, Andrew B. Newman, Gwen C. Rudie, William Schoenell, Patricio Schurter, Stephen Smee, Jason E. Williams
Items.Title: Implementing a documentation library for MIRMOS
Items.Abstract: We describe the implementation of a documentation library for the Magellan InfraRed Multi-Object Spectrograph (MIRMOS) development team. The need for a unified documentation library was identified as a priority for the MIRMOS project very early into concept development phase. The implementation process started with a definition of use cases and requirements that resulted in a tool choice and subsequent implementation. The library now hosts hundreds of documents; it is widely used by our team and supports our document release process. In this paper, we describe the process of implementation of the document library to support our documentation management plan, as well as a description of the library, some of its most used functionality and some usage statistics. Our implementation is a low-cost solution for a mid-scale instrument team.
